I fly all over the world for work. Here are my tips:

  1. Noise reduction headphones, get them, make sure you have enough batteries for them. This is the single best thing to improve the experience.

  2. Get a Coccyx memory foam seat cushion.

  3. Bring healthy snacks in small sealed bags (like 100 cal almonds, Dried fruit, that sort of ting). The sealed small bags get through any security.

  4. Get a neck pillow and put them on backwards. Let your chin fall forward into the pillow, at least for me this significantly decreases neck aches.

  5. If you can afford it (heck even if you can't try to save a bit more and do it anyway), upgrade at the gate, better rates and sometimes you even get bumped higher. The long flight economy + is like the 80's first class, pretty nice and have leg rests. Oh and the meal comes on actual plates.

  6. Order a special meal, they tend to be better than general fair.

  7. Hydrate, Hydrate Hydrate.

  8. Bring a roll of TP with you, generally much better quality and you know you have it.

  9. One small pad, 7" with kindle and lot's of storage. Load it up with books, TV, movies and music think how you can be entertained without being online. One pad that can act as a laptop replacement for meetings and such if one is working. Leave the laptop at home unless there is no other way. I check mine in if I need it, never had an issue, but it can get stolen. I use TSA locks, but that doesn't protect much.

  10. Take it slow, easy and pace yourself, don't worry so much about queues, leave yourself plenty of time.

  11. Outside the US, most places take the local airlines over a US carrier, cost is generally less and service is generally better.

For Security:

  1. Wear elastic waist pants so no belt to mess with.

  2. Wear slip on shoes

  3. Cary only a backpack (I have the backpack with rollers), it is much easier to put away and deal with when you have been traveling 20 hours or more.

  4. Carry nothing in your pockets but your Travel docs, passport, cash and CC.

  5. Have everything ready to go so you are not that guy holding up the line.

  6. Smile and be polite to officials, they are doing a tough job and you are more likely to get their help or even extras if you are kind. I had one security lady stop a woman who was rude to me after cutting in the queue, held her to do a search. She looked directly at me and winked. Heh.

It is pretty easy to get a script for 6 Xanax from your doctor for air travel. If you've never had it before, though, try it a couple of days before you leave to see how it affects you. Do not drink alcohol while on a benzo.

My preferred coctail is a Benadryl and Dramamine an hour before flight, repeat just before takeoff, then a whiskey on the first drink service. That knocks me out until food service, and repeat the dosage. Also, I wear sunglasses all through flight, they may not disguise the fact that you are asleep (vulnerable) but they don't advertise it like sleep masks do.

This will sound odd, cowboy boot that slip off and on. This comes in handy at the security check points. Slip boots off, stuff all pocket material into boots which go through x-ray. Once on the other side reverse all that and you're gone. It's quick and all your shit is in that boot.
yeah, make sure some idiot doesn't inflate the main life raft thereby delaying your flight for 4 hours

drink.

load up[ your phone or tablet with a variety of tv shows or movies and some podcasts.

Nothing that you do will make the flight shorter. Remember that.

Leave late at night. Falling asleep is easier when you are already tired. Lots of different distractions: books comics, movies puzzles, something new. once you learn to isolate noise, and just accept it... its not that bad...

i can also stay up indefinitely, but shit starts to get weird at bout day three. your body/gut starts saying wtf
Have a buddy who is constantly flying everywhere. He really likes the Samsung vr for watching movies. That with a nice set of headphones.
Also...I had a friend and client die of the results of deep vein thrombosis. Get up and walk around every hour or two. No matter what.

An eyemask, earplugs, and neck pillow for the flight. No caffeine! Sleep so jetlag isnt a big deal.

Drink lots of fluids (planes are dry), prepay for all checked luggage (keep it under 50lbs or 20something kilos), and make your carryon small. Like a small laptop bag that can hold a book, battery bank, and minor essentials, and is small/light enough you could throw it like a frisbee.

If you have a long layover anywhere, buy a tshirt and change shirts. Yes, you just paid $15-20 for a shirt. BUT you now smell and feel better, and it's worth it.

xanax is always a big help, but only if you know how it affects you in what quantities, the last thing you want is to be disfunctional and lost when you land if you're not used to it / if you fly out of the country a lot get a global entry card, you need to set up a background check and meeting with FBI agents, but its really worth it to skip all customs and lines getting back into the states by swiping a card at the machine (bonus you can also activate it online to work as a nexus card for when you travel to canada and back, you hold it up to an infrared scanner before you hit the border and they already have all your info which makes it a lot easier)
Buy a bottle of whisky in the airport for carry on, finish it before you land.

Drink lots of water, take a laxative (and do your business), and eat something healthy and fibrous (like a salad) well before your flight. Nobody wants to have a war in their belly during an intercontinental flight. Leave your seat for stretching, washing up, and a quick whiz.
I've done 5+ hour flights. I hated it. If I did another I'd stay up the entire night and just sleep through the first part.

Booze. Don't get shitfaced but anytime you feel like you are sobering up even a tad get another beer. Generally I start out with mix drinks at the airport bar and then beers on the flight.

Normally I only drink once a year. I wouldn't drink at all anymore but I like the christmas beers. I also love the two week holiday festivally atmosphere. But other than that I hate booze and avoid it.

But if I HAVE to fly I'm getting loose as shit before and during. If I survive I get a lavish meal.
